issues.claim: On most maps, Greenland looks as big as Africa
issues.problem: Sources say this of the Mercator projection specifically; 'most maps' is a generalization (true of wall/web maps, not of equal-area maps). Africa 30.37M km2 / Greenland 2.166M km2 = 14.0, so the 14x figure checks out.
issues.fix: On a Mercator map, Greenland looks as big as Africa, but Africa is fourteen times larger.

issues.problem: Precisely, it shows lines of constant compass bearing (rhumb lines) as straight lines; 'compass lines' is loose but not misleading.
issues.fix: Mercator's 1569 map drew constant-bearing courses as straight lines, and paid with swollen land near the poles.

issues.problem: Rhetorical; supported in substance (every flat projection distorts; none is both equal-area and conformal), but 'lie' is stylistic.
issues.fix: Every flat map picks its distortion, so giant Greenland is a trade, not a mistake.
